Criterion (A) was demonstrated on THIS board on 2026-09-02 (scripts/vessl_cv06b_estimator_falsifiers.yaml, VESSL 369367257702, exit 0; pre-2.0 realization: 1.453 % / 0.9684 / 0.3175 bin / 46.48 Ω) and re-measured on the sheet-declared board on 2026-09-07 (VESSL 369367259191, exit 0), whose summary is the committed one: `validation/crossval/_06b_msl_notch_results/cv06b_build_falsifiers_summary.json::criterion_A_baseline.err_pct = 2.1649`, `validation/crossval/_06b_msl_notch_results/cv06b_build_falsifiers_summary.json::criterion_A_baseline.bw_ratio = 0.9991`, `validation/crossval/_06b_msl_notch_results/cv06b_build_falsifiers_summary.json::criterion_A_baseline.witness_bins = 0.4469`, `validation/crossval/_06b_msl_notch_results/cv06b_build_falsifiers_summary.json::criterion_A_baseline.z0_median_ohm = 48.19`. ONE PRE-DECLARED FALSIFIER FIRED on the pre-2.0 board and is recorded, not softened: a one-cell stub-length error (analytic shift `validation/crossval/_06b_msl_notch_results/cv06b_build_falsifiers_summary.json::stub_1cell.true_shift_pct = 0.532` %, 0.30 bin) moved the refined notch estimate by only 0.145 % (the bin argmin: 0.000 %), below the declared half-of-predicted visibility criterion; not attributed (estimator under-response on a -43.5 dB, one-bin-wide null vs a physical shift smaller than the closed form). Neither the under- nor the over-response is attributed and the finer-DFT experiment is still owed; visibility is not an accuracy statement. G1's verdict does not rest on sub-bin resolution (a full-bin error is 1.75 %; 2.16 + 1.75 = 3.91 < 4.0, 0.09 pp of margin where the pre-2.0 board had 0.80). The CPU-side detection-power evidence, including the geometry-built shallow-notch ladder that replaced a near-circular round-1 construction, is tests/fixtures/cv06b_estimator_regate/cv06b_estimator_falsifiers.json (keys case_A_baseline, case_B_sub_bin_ladder, case_C_shallow_notch_from_geometry, case_D_quantised_estimator). The committed matched-geometry dx=50 um OpenEMS/E4 artifacts in artifact_paths are NOT the same board as this script solves post-#723: this script's own substrate now realizes h_sub=254um exactly, while the E4 rfx leg (scripts/diagnostics/build_msl_notch_rfx_dx50.py, deferred, not fixed by #723) still realizes h_sub=300um at its own dx=50um. Treat the E4/OpenEMS comparison as characterizing a DIFFERENT (300um) board until that script is also fixed. Not a broad MSL-port claim. LATTICE OWNERSHIP CONTRACT (#931, 2026-09-07): the metal is declared as two zero-thickness SHEETS on the substrate-top node plane (z = 254 µm); each realizes 10 node rows, i.e. a GEOMETRIC extent of 571.5 µm (the node span `fidelity_report` prints) and an ELECTRICAL width of 635.0 µm (n_rows·dx, what the Hammerstad-Jensen reference takes). The pre-#931 rule reported 635.0 µm as the geometric extent because it zeroed one edge past each footprint's hi rim. The substrate row is bit-identical (dielectric sampling is fenced, design note §1.8), so "h_sub=254um exactly" stands. Every criterion-A and criterion-B value quoted above is re-read by JSON path from the re-solved run (VESSL 369367259191) at ingest, not translated; the G4 Re(Z0) median (46.48 ± 1.0 Ω on the committed run) is the pre-declared falsifier for the electrical-width convention — a median near 49.4 Ω would flip it to the 571.5 µm reading. No window moved (NOTCH_FREQ_TOL_PCT 4.0, STOPBAND_BW_FRAC_IDEAL 0.210274, BW ratio 0.80–1.20). Re-solved as VESSL run 369367259191. The pre-declared falsifier was G4's Z0 median: ~46.5 Ω would say the electrical width of an n-row strip is n·dx = 635.0 µm, ~49.4 Ω would say it is the geometric node span (n−1)·dx = 571.5 µm. Measured 48.192 Ω -- between them, 4.35 % above HJ(635.0) = 46.18 and 2.43 % below HJ(571.5) = 49.39. BOTH readings are rejected and the convention is NOT settled. Three more pre-declarations were falsified with it: the notch rose +3.67 % (3.7586 GHz) where one stub cell predicted +0.51 %, `err_pct` rose 1.4530 -> 2.1649 % where ≈0.95 % was predicted, and the half-grid witness and notch depth moved (0.3175 -> 0.4469 bin, −43.3 -> −39.44 dB) where neither was predicted to. All four gates still PASS on their own unchanged windows (G1 2.16 % < 4.0 %, G2 0.9991, G3 0.4469 bin, G4 48.2 Ω) and NOTHING is re-derived from the measurement: one board at one dx cannot settle an effective-width convention. The case still ships n·dx and both named quantities stay named. Criterion B now closes -- the one-cell stub arm went `visible: false -> true` and `verdict.all_ok false -> true`. Headline for this mesh is now 2.16 % / −39.4 dB / 48.2 Ω, superseding 1.40 / 43.3 / 46.5.

cases.claim_scope: CHARACTERIZATION ONLY of the Sheen 1990 stepped-impedance LPF stopband — explicitly NOT an rfx accuracy claim. The Palace-FEM referee showed the stopband is a DOUBLE transmission zero (~7.0 and ~8.0 GHz): openEMS resolves both and matches Palace to ~0.7%; the referee records sides_with=openems. HISTORY: the original num_periods=20 default-offset rfx leg was non-passive (58/120 bins, worst column power 1794.5 at 17.05 GHz) and its argmin (7.218 GHz) sat 9.6% from openEMS. Root cause was MEASURED for the truncation half (settling witness -24.7/-24.3 dB; the probe near-field half is measured in PR #468) and the leg regenerated 2026-07-26 with num_periods=60 + n_probe_offset=30 (satisfies BOTH the 5*h_sub near-field clearance and the lambda_g/4 reflector clearance that offset=40 violated) + passivity-enforced S. REGENERATED AGAIN 2026-08-09 (issue #519) on the #511/#507-corrected extractor (PR #516, f95240f): witness -70.2/-71.3 dB, strict ||S||_2 <= 1 at every bin (max column power 0.9995), and the raw passivity excess COLLAPSED (0/120 bins > 0.05, worst 0.0145 at 17.38 GHz; the pre-#516 leg's 84/120 bins worst 0.365 was substantially the extractor defects, not a coarse-mesh envelope). With decontaminated probes the rfx argmin lands at 7.874 GHz — the ~8 GHz doublet member, 1.4% from openEMS — confirming the referee's doublet structure; sides_with=openems stands (structure distance 1.52% vs openEMS 0.66%, re-derived by build_sheen_lpf_palace_referee.py on the regenerated leg). Passband mean |S21| agrees with openEMS to 0.0014 (was 0.0156), and the old ~67 ohm passband Re(Z0) fit residual is gone (50.3 ohm passband, 52.4 ohm in-band). The argmin null POSITION and passband/stopband STRUCTURE are the readable outputs; any bin with correction > 0.05 (none on the current leg) is artifact-class for magnitude claims. Gates lock (A) openEMS reference sanity comparator-first, (B) comparison shape, (C) the committed argmin nulls + rfx passband mean + referee verdict, and (D) the evidence chain: strict bound, settling witness, and the passivity-correction footprint (fail-closed D0 if a leg lacks the witness/enforcement fields). RE-GATED 2026-09-01 (issue #812 mechanism P3, docs/design_notes/estimator_resolution_regate.md): C1's bin argmin was quantised at 2.081%/bin against a declared 1% window, so C4-C7 were added -- sub-bin log-parabolic locks on both doublet members for both solvers (+-0.50%, against the committed referee fixture's own fdtd_doublet_ghz), a transmission-zero COUNT gate (== 2 at <= -20 dB), a -3 dB corner-frequency lock (+-0.25%) on a quantity this case never gated, and an in-run half-grid resolution witness. Nothing was widened; C1 is kept unchanged. Criteria (A) and (B) both measured on the committed legs: tests/fixtures/cv07_estimator_regate/cv07_estimator_falsifiers.json (keys baseline, defects.erased_zero, defects.corner_m20, window_derivations). LATTICE OWNERSHIP CONTRACT (#931, 2026-09-07): the three conductors are SHEETS on one node plane instead of three one-cell Boxes (which the contract would realize as a 200 µm slab with two walls). Realized at dx = 200 µm: sheet plane z = 800 µm (= the realized laminate face; declared foil plane 794 µm, +6.0 µm, no vacuum slot), both 50-Ω feeds 2200 µm wide over 12 node rows, patch 20200 × 2400 µm. Pre-#931 the same board reported 2400 / 20400 / 2600 µm — one cell more on every in-plane extent, the rim edge the old rule zeroed. The strips' current-carrying row counts are unchanged, so their electrical widths are unchanged. The port mismatch recorded in the script is re-measured and still OPEN: each port spans 13 node rows while its feed metal realizes 12; closing it needs §1.9 core work (the port taking its cross-section from the realized sheet footprint), because passing the port the contract's realized extent would set the wave split's reference to HJ(2200, 800) = 54.22 Ω on a line this case measures at 50.30 Ω. Every rfx-leg figure recited above is re-read from the re-solved run (VESSL 369367259192) at ingest; C4 (±0.50 %) and C6 (±0.25 %) are not widened — both derive from the cell size, which did not change. Re-solved as VESSL run 369367259192; every COMMITTED rfx entry is re-pinned from its produced `rfx.json` with no gate window moved (argmin null 7.8739 -> 8.2017 GHz, doublet (6.943990, 7.925928) -> (7.233338, 8.244069), corner 5.5036 -> 5.7071, passband mean 0.9378 -> 0.9471). The Palace referee fixture was re-derived by its own producer; `sides_with` stays 'openems' and rfx's structure distance goes 1.52 % -> 2.87 %. QUOTABILITY, WORSE AND NOT ABSORBED: bins carrying a raw passivity correction > 0.05 went 0 -> 3 and the worst went 0.0145 @ 17.378 GHz -> 0.6572 @ 17.870 GHz. All three sit above 17 GHz and none inside the 5–15 GHz null band, so gate D5 and the in-band footprint are unchanged; no magnitude claim above 15 GHz is made or permitted. FOOTPRINT VS DOUBLET-MARGIN (2026-09-10, issue #964): two of the dimensions that set the LPF cutoff are realized off-lattice beyond a filter's tolerance under EITHER width convention -- patch propagation length declared 2540.0 um, realized 2400.0 um (geometric node span, -5.51%) or 2600.0 um (electrical n*dx, +2.36%); feed width declared 2413.0 um, realized 2200.0 um (-8.83%) or 2400.0 um (-0.54%); neither convention is settled (#729) and gcd(2540, 794, 2413, 20320) = 1 um (`validation/crossval/07_sheen_lpf.py`'s own docstring) means no practical dx lands every load-bearing dimension on-lattice. `assert_realized_metal` (`validation/crossval/07_sheen_lpf.py`) does not compare these to their declared values. The case's gate surface pins all four exactly, not merely printing them: `tests/crossval/test_cv07_realized_metal.py` (`test_sheet_sits_on_the_realized_laminate_face` pins plane_z, `test_both_50_ohm_feeds_realize_the_same_width` pins feed_w, `test_realized_patch_is_one_cell_under_declared_on_each_axis` pins patch_trv and patch_prop), each `pytest.approx(rel=1e-12)`, already in this case's gate_paths -- a dx change, a moved lattice origin, or an edited declaration fails that suite. MARGIN THE DOUBLET CLAIM ACTUALLY RESTS ON, measured not assumed: the Palace referee's two doublet members sit `tests/fixtures/sheen_lpf_e4/sheen_lpf_palace_referee.json::referee.palace_doublet_mid_ghz.lower = 7.031752` to `tests/fixtures/sheen_lpf_e4/sheen_lpf_palace_referee.json::referee.palace_doublet_mid_ghz.upper = 8.048223` GHz apart (1.016471 GHz, 12.63% of the upper member), and rfx's identified null (`tests/fixtures/sheen_lpf_e4/sheen_lpf_palace_referee.json::referee.fdtd_doublet_ghz.rfx.argmin_first_null_ghz = 8.244069`) differs from Palace's SAME (upper) member by 2.433% -- 19.3% of that spacing, roughly a 5.5x margin. A naive single-dimension estimate (f ~ 1/L applied to the -5.51% propagation-length error alone) predicts a ~5.8% shift, 46% of the spacing -- more than double the measured total, and the two DO NOT COMPOSE: the naive estimate and the measured total disagree by roughly 3.4 percentage points of unexplained cancellation, isolated by no leg in this record. The doublet-member identification holds on this board, by a real measured margin -- but that margin's own size is not explained by the one geometry defect this record names, and a future mesh or geometry change could remove whatever produces the current cancellation without touching the dimension the margin is attributed to -- the consequence would be a regression that fires for a reason nobody predicted. Read the 5.5x figure as an observation, not as headroom anyone has earned.

MERGE OF TWO INDEPENDENT FIXES (2026-09-10): main issue #920 (the rfx probe post floated between the two conductors, touching neither -- closes #920) and this branch's issue #931 (the lattice ownership contract: BOTH conductors declared SHEETS -- zero-thickness PEC `Box`es on the two substrate faces, the same structure both openEMS legs build; before #931 the ground was a one-cell PEC Box drawn below the floor and flagged `two_plane=True` (issue #706) so a second wall landed on z_sub_lo, and #931 deletes the flag along with the volume declaration it patched). These are NOT two compounding changes: #920's derivation (the port spans from the ground Box's realized corner to the patch Box's) and #931's independently-chosen full-substrate feed (`z_sub_lo -> z_sub_hi`) are algebraically the SAME span once both conductors are sheets, because a sheet's `corner_lo` and `corner_hi` coincide -- verified by measurement, not assumed: the merged code reproduces the pre-merge #931 leg's settling witness bit-for-bit (-68.69142333390357 dB). `assert_galvanic_feed`/`_feed_check_ok` (#920) had to be RESPELT for sheets: a sheet's normal E component never goes PEC (design note §1.3, "normal E through a sheet stays live"), so #920's original first/last-cell-dead criterion is unsatisfiable on this board and was replaced with a plane criterion -- the feed's two endpoints must themselves be realized conductor wall planes, read through the SAME `realized_pec_edge_masks`/`realized_wall_planes` pair `assert_realized_stack` uses. `assert_realized_stack()` reads the contract's one edge set and refuses to quote f0 unless the realized wall planes over the patch footprint are EXACTLY {z_sub_lo, z_sub_hi} -- no wall at k_patch+1 -- and the assembled eps_r still holds exactly the two declared values, a sheet owning no cell and writing no material. MEASURED on the merged leg (VESSL 369367260032): rfx reads 3.99 % HIGH vs openEMS (2.4230 vs 2.330 GHz) and +0.31 % vs the analytic anchor, openEMS -3.54 %. The two solvers no longer sit on the same side of the closed form -- rfx reads high, openEMS low -- and the rfx-vs-openEMS distance grew from 0.69 % to 3.99 % while the rfx-vs-analytic distance shrank from -4.21 % to +0.31 %; the openEMS leg did not move. The S11 dip deepened from -4.4 dB to -19.0 dB against openEMS's -20.1 dB, off-resonance max|S11| went from 0.787 to 0.991 against openEMS's 0.992, and the ring-down Q fell from 18.9 to 10.1: the feed now reaches the conductor instead of coupling capacitively. A decomposition run on the pre-merge #931-only base (production sheets with the PRE-#931 feed, VESSL 369367259279, `_15_patch_results/rfx_decomposition_feed_pre931.json`) splits the +4.71 % into 58 % / 42 % -- from the #768 leg to sheets with the pre-#931 feed is +2.74 % (2.3139 → 2.3774 GHz, Q 18.9 → 18.3), and from there to the full-span feed a further +1.92 % (2.3774 → 2.4230 GHz, Q 18.3 → 10.1, and essentially all of the Q collapse). It lands in stage_b.cross_solver_report as signed_beta_envelope_lo_frac, signed_beta_envelope_hi_frac, signed_beta_envelope_terms, signed_beta_envelope_witness_openems, signed_beta_envelope_witness_rfx and signed_beta_envelope_cross_solver_summary; the two witnesses and the cross-solver summary carry gated=false and reported_only_issue=830 (the lo/hi floats and the terms dict are bare values), none raises, and none is wired into sanity_passed. The witness key offset_from_thickness_corrected_prediction_frac records how far each solver's mean signed deviation sits from the line both sign-definite corrections predict, and half_cell_rasterization_band_frac is reported beside the envelope so an excursion smaller than this mesh's half-cell rasterization ambiguity is NOT attributed to solver physics without a second dx. ISSUE #812 P1 RE-GATE (2026-09-01): every leg listed above as GATED is intra-run self-consistency -- each solver's angle(S21) against THAT SAME solver's own measured beta -- so a COHERENT phase-velocity error (beta and angle(S21) moved together) cancels identically. TWO INDEPENDENT-REFERENCE GATES ADDED, both wired into sanity_passed, neither widening anything: (E2) each solver's measured beta against the Hammerstad-Jensen quasi-static closed form of the REALIZED board, tolerance 2.0% -- pre-declared as the linear sum of HJ model accuracy (0.50% in beta), the one-cell conductor thickness the zero-thickness form omits (1.21%, Bahl-Garg) and neglected dispersion at the band top (0.06%, Getsinger) = 1.77%, rounded up one step; measured 0.938% (rfx) and 0.307% (openEMS) on run-2, 0.494% (openEMS, declared board) on run-1. (E4) the RAW cross-solver angle(S21) difference -- previously REPORTED, NOW GATED -- at 3.0 deg, pre-declared as one-cell h_sub (0.3176 deg) + one-cell w_trace (0.1459 deg) + this file's own committed +-4-cell reference-plane budget (1.787 deg) = 2.2505 deg, rounded up one step; measured 0.3418 deg (run-2) and 0.3039 deg (run-1). Derivations: docs/design_notes/issue812_phase_identity_predeclaration.md and the script's own EXTERNAL_PHASE_REFERENCE_PREDECLARATION. No physics verdict changed. ISSUE #830 (audit G1, 2026-09-02) ADDS ONE REPORTED, NOT GATED LEG, registered as this case's fourth reference: the SIGNED runtime-derived beta envelope described there. It reports, it does not gate -- sanity_passed and every tolerance above are byte-identical -- and on the committed run-2 artifact it flags the rfx side above hi while openEMS sits inside, an excess SMALLER than the same board's half-cell rasterization band, so the witness reports that ambiguity rather than resolving it. Resolving it needs a second dx, which has not been run. LATTICE OWNERSHIP CONTRACT (#931, 2026-09-07). The rfx-side trace is a VOLUME: the 1-cell PEC Box in the fixture producer is drawn unchanged and now realizes tangential walls at BOTH of its faces (z = 250 and 300 um at dx = 50 um), a one-cell metal thickness, which is what openEMS Stage B already built. Before the contract rfx realized a single wall plane with Ez live through the metal, so this case's `conductor_thickness_one_cell` tolerance term (0.0121, 68% of B_BETA_ANALYTIC_TOL_FRAC) bounded a difference rfx did not have. The term's VALUE is unchanged and its DERIVATION was re-declared before the re-solve; had the contract made rfx's realized thickness zero the term would have been deleted, not re-tuned. The sheet alternative was measured and rejected: 254 um is off-lattice at dx = 50 um, a sheet snaps to the 250 um node and leaves 50 um of realized laminate above the strip (a buried strip, not this board), and its realized width is 550 um against the drawn 600 um. Redrawing on-lattice (dx = h_sub/5 = 50.8 um) stays rejected for this lane's own recorded reason: it destroys the on-lattice `ref_plane_shift`. Both the rfx fixture and the openEMS Stage B artifact are superseded, not patched (producer run VESSL 369367259200; the fixture and the re-run Stage B are committed at ingest). `meta['trace_y_lo/hi_realized_m']` move one cell (950/1550 -> 900/1500 um) and `meta` gains `trace_wall_planes_realized`, `trace_wall_planes_realized_z_m`, `trace_realization_kind` and `t_metal_realized_m`; `h_sub_realized_m` (300 um), `n_z_sub_realized` (6) and `w_trace_realized_m` (600 um) do not move. Stage B asserts its own metal thickness against `t_metal_realized_m` rather than stating the equality in prose. The regenerated fixture was ingested on 2026-09-07 (VESSL 369367259200); the `beta` residuals quoted above (0.94% rfx, 0.31% openEMS) are the pre-#931 record and remain the reading of the committed run-1/run-2 artifacts, whose stored `beta_rfx_real` is the pre-contract fixture's. On the re-solved fixture the rfx E2 leg reads 0.31% openEMS / 1.41% rfx and the E4 raw cross-solver phase reads 0.5308 deg (was 0.3418), a margin of 5.7x rather than 8.8x. E2 judges each solver against the board THAT solver builds, which #931 made two different boards under the strip: 250 um of dielectric under rfx's inlaid one-cell volume trace, 300 um under openEMS's strip proud on top. Neither tolerance moved; the pre-declared analytic budget was re-derived at 250 um and got tighter against its gate (sum 0.0177 -> 0.0185 under an unchanged 0.0200). cases.claim_scope: Issue #489 stage 3, promoted 2026-08-04 (PI decision, issue #489 comment https://github.com/bk-squared/rfx/issues/489#issuecomment-5179893223; evidence = run-3 VESSL 369367251629 plus an offline fix verified by replaying run-3's own committed field data through tests/crossval/test_coax_two_port_referee_header.py's regression suite -- no re-run needed). One through-line geometry: rfx's own SMA-class coaxial_port fixture (pin radius a=0.635mm, outer-conductor inner radius b=2.055mm, PTFE eps_r=2.1, L12=58.4595mm feed-to-feed span), one mesh (dx=0.37474mm, rfx's own auto-derived Yee cell at freq_max=40GHz), two drives (forward port-1-driven and reverse port-2-driven, giving the full S-matrix). This is staircase dispersion (the referral hypothesis is ruled out by the implied-length mismatch matching no candidate discrete referral-cell count) from this coax's own coarse a-to-b PTFE annulus (measured/analytic beta ratio ~1.12x, 1.1205-1.1212 across the gated central band, 1.1202-1.1222 across the full 4-12GHz sweep; ~3.8 cells across (2.055-0.635mm)/0.37474mm), NOW MEASURED BY A MESH-REFINEMENT CONVERGENCE WITNESS (issue #489 leg 1, VESSL 369367251845, 2026-08-05, pre-declared one-sided acceptance band before the run per this repo's R2 discipline): a 1.5x mesh refinement (annulus 3.79->5.68 cells, dx 0.37474mm->0.24983mm) moves the measured/analytic beta ratio from 1.1208 to 1.0661624823818885 (per-bin range 1.0660627719113418-1.0662474785033922 across the gated central band -- essentially flat), implied convergence order p=1.4847707054524188 (two-point, from this single 1.5x step -- not a multi-level fit; between the naive first-order O(dx) lower bound this predeclaration's excess-scaling estimate assumed and second-order O(dx^2) -- consistent with openEMS's own material averaging at a dielectric interface, not a fault narrative) -- the pre-declared one-sided acceptance band (refutes only ratio > 1.11) CONFIRMED. See validation/crossval/21_coax_two_port_referee.py's MESH_REFINEMENT_PREDECLARATION and the committed validation/crossval/_21_coax_two_port_referee_logs/mesh_refinement_369367251845_result.json for the full per-bin evidence. The four agreeing beta readings (port1/port2, both drives, ~0.01% mutual agreement) AT THE ORIGINAL MESH DENSITY remain ONE witness, not four -- same run, same solver, same CalcPort extractor (this repo's own agreement-is-not-independence rule); the mesh-refinement witness above is the independent second axis that rule calls for. REPORTED, NOT GATED: run-3's own |S21|~=1.000 (0.99997-1.00003 across the full 4-12GHz sweep, both drives) for this independent, differently-discretized openEMS geometry -- consistent with, not a refutation of, rfx's own PR #534 raw 0.960->0.737 decline (attributed there to rfx's own numerical staircase attenuation, a DIFFERENT geometry/discretization); reciprocity (|S21| vs |S12|, max mag dev 1.2e-5, max phase dev 0.0012deg -- essentially exact for this passive, matched-mesh fixture). UPDATE (2026-08-06, issue #489 final PI decision): compute_coaxial_two_port's own EXPERIMENTAL label was lifted separately, using this referee as one leg of its evidence chain (alongside a mesh-refinement convergence witness and an AD gate) -- see docs/guides/sparameter_support_matrix.md for the current VALIDATED WITH SCOPE statement; this referee's own scope fence (brackets, does not judge) is unchanged. Does not characterize a different geometry, mesh density, coax-planar transition, AD, or the reverse_drive call-site wiring (the active #489 dev track). ISSUE #812 P1 RE-GATE (2026-09-01): Stage B's phase/group-delay witness compares unwrap(angle(S21)) against -beta_measured*L12 with beta_measured from the SAME field solve, so a COHERENT phase-velocity error cancels identically -- the #812 audit measured max_phase_dev EXACTLY 0.000 deg and gd_dev EXACTLY 0.00 ps at k = 1.02/1.10/1.30/1.50/1.57 against the 30 deg / 200 ps gate. ONE INDEPENDENT-REFERENCE GATE ADDED (E2, _analytic_beta_witness, wired into sanity_passed, widening nothing): the port's measured beta AND the group delay measured from S21 alone, against the EXACT continuum coax TEM values 2*pi*f*sqrt(eps_r)/c0 and L12*sqrt(eps_r)/c0 -- a reference side containing no quantity from the run. Its envelope is mesh-dependent because this fixture's ~12% staircase bias is real and convergent: BOUND(N) = 1.30 * 0.1208 * (3.789/N)**1.4847707054524188, with the form and both scale numbers taken verbatim from the committed MESH_REFINEMENT_PREDECLARATION (2026-08-04, VESSL 369367251845) and only the 1.30 headroom declared new. Unlike a round-up(measured x 1.5) width this envelope TIGHTENS as the mesh refines: 0.157022 at the registered mesh, 0.086002 at the committed 1.5x refinement. Criterion (A), replayed on committed field data at BOTH meshes: registered mesh beta dev 0.121179 and group-delay dev 0.125221 against bound 0.157022; refined mesh 0.066247 and 0.067494 against 0.086002. Criterion (B): a coherent k=1.57 perturbation reds it at beta dev 0.760250 (and through the real _run_stage_b wiring, not the witness alone), while the old witness's deviation stays bit-identical to its unperturbed 0.4365 deg at every k. DECLARED DETECTION FLOOR, stated rather than discovered: k > 1.032334 or k < 0.752106 at the registered mesh -- the audit's k=1.02 is BELOW it, because no honest analytic gate on a 3.8-cell annulus can be tighter than the staircase bias itself. CORRECTION (round-2 review, 2026-09-02): the floor as declared is the 1.30 HEADROOM's choice, not the annulus's -- headroom 1.10 would put it at `validation/crossval/_issue812_phase_identity/regate_evidence.json::cv21.detection_floor.headroom_dependence[1].k_hi = 1.010778` with criterion (A) intact, and the physics-forced floor at this mesh is `validation/crossval/_issue812_phase_identity/regate_evidence.json::cv21.detection_floor.physics_forced_registered.k_hi = 1.003945`; HEADROOM is not tightened post hoc. Refining the mesh moves the floor with no change to the gate. EVIDENCE-LEVEL CORRECTION (revised 2026-09-01, round-2 review -- round 1's version of this paragraph, which kept E4 on the argument that it covered Stage A's tutorial reproduce-gate, is WITHDRAWN): NO leg in this case is E4 and evidence_levels is now [E1, E2]. E4 in docs/guides/physics_validation_evidence_rule.md is the same geometry compared against an external full-wave solver, and the refuting search was run rather than skipped -- this script imports no rfx module and reads no rfx fixture, so no leg here puts an rfx quantity on either side of a comparison; Stage A compares openEMS against Coax.m's own closed form, which is an analytic check ON the external solver, not a cross-solver check OF rfx. The E4 comparison this referee's openEMS output feeds lives DOWNSTREAM, in the compute_coaxial_two_port label-lift chain recorded in docs/guides/sparameter_support_matrix.json, which is where the cross-solver claim about rfx is actually made. Stage B's gated phase claim is E2 (analytic beta) plus E1 (self-consistency, kept and unchanged, now labelled E1 in the artifact's own evidence_level field). CRITERION (A) RESTATED (2026-09-01, round-2 review): the ~1.30x beta margin is the declared headroom BY CONSTRUCTION at BOTH meshes and the refined-mesh check is arithmetically the registered-mesh statement, not an independent confirmation -- the committed convergence order IS the two-point fit through the two committed excesses, so the refined-mesh envelope equals the headroom times that mesh's own committed excess to `validation/crossval/_issue812_phase_identity/regate_evidence.json::cv21.margin_is_the_declared_headroom_by_construction.bound_at_n_after_minus_headroom_times_excess_after` with a recovered-order error of `validation/crossval/_issue812_phase_identity/regate_evidence.json::cv21.margin_is_the_declared_headroom_by_construction.order_p_recovery_abs_error = 0`. LATTICE OWNERSHIP CONTRACT (#931): OUT OF SCOPE and unchanged. rfx's coax pin and shell are a sigma stamp (`stamp_coaxial_line` writes PEC_SIGMA into `materials.sigma`), which design note section 1.8 fences out of the contract as a lossy-volume model; they never enter `pec_mask` or the realized edge set. No geometry moves and no committed artifact is invalidated. What the contract does NOT resolve stays recorded rather than half-migrated: the shell spanning [b - dz, b], `r_os = b + 2*dx`, and `B_Z0_OHM` computed on the nominal a-to-b annulus are all compensations for a conductor model that has no declared realization at all. That is the follow-up issue section 1.8 names.
